meta.title: Invoice exceptions, resolved before lunch
meta.tagline: An agent that reads a blocked supplier invoice, finds why it does not match the order, and hands the clerk a decision instead of a search. **Example content: replace every value.**

hero.label: from a blocked invoice to a decision the clerk can approve
hero.source: Timed on 12 real exceptions by the accounts payable lead; the 20 minutes is the target of the proof of concept.
hero.note: Twelve exceptions timed by hand in September.

problem.headline: One invoice in six stops, and each stop costs **three days**
problem.lead: When an invoice does not match its purchase order, a clerk becomes a detective: three systems, two mailboxes and a buyer who is in a meeting.
problem.who: Four accounts payable clerks and the 30 buyers they chase for answers.
problem.today: The clerk opens the ERP, the order, the goods receipt and the supplier's email, compares them by eye, then writes to the buyer and waits.
problem.cost: About 310 blocked invoices a month. Late payment fees and lost early-payment discounts follow the delay.
problem.why_now: The supplier base grew by a third this year and the team did not.

facts.label: of invoices stop on a mismatch
of the three days is waiting for a reply

problem.quote: I do not need help paying invoices. I need help finding out why I cannot.

process.headline: Nine steps and four hand-offs become **four steps and two**
process.lead: The redesign does not make the detective faster. It removes the detective work: the evidence is gathered before a person looks.
process.source: before: 12 exceptions timed by the accounts payable lead; after: the target the proof of concept is built to meet

steps.title: Reads the block and gathers the evidence
Names the cause and drafts the fix
Releases the invoice, logs the reason

architecture.headline: Bob builds it, watsonx Orchestrate runs it, the ERP stays where it is
architecture.lead: Nothing in the company's systems is replaced. The agent reads through two narrow tools and writes through one, and that one waits for a person.
architecture.caption: Dashed nodes are mocked in the proof of concept with synthetic data; the interfaces are the real ones, so the mock is swapped for the system later.

nodes.title: Chat
nodes.role: the chat the buyer answers in

nodes.title: Triage agent
nodes.role: runs the triage and resolver agents and their tools

nodes.title: Granite
nodes.role: reads invoices and writes the explanation

nodes.title: Decision log
nodes.role: keeps every decision and its reason

decisions.title: Two agents, not one
decisions.why: Triage only reads. The resolver is the one agent that can write, so the approval step guards a single door.

decisions.title: Mocks behind real interfaces
decisions.why: The proof of concept runs on synthetic invoices. No company data leaves the company, and the mock is replaced by the ERP adapter in the pilot.

decisions.title: Built in Bob from the first line
decisions.why: The plan, the tools, the agent definitions and the tests come from one Bob task history, which is also what the judges read.

impact.headline: The clerk's hour stays an hour. The **three days of waiting** go.

waterfall.title: Where the yearly value comes from

items.label: Clerk hours returned
items.source: 310 a month × 63 min × loaded hourly cost

items.label: Buyer hours returned
items.source: 40 min on half of the exceptions

items.label: Late fees avoided
items.source: fees paid in the last 12 months

items.label: Run cost
items.source: platform and model usage at pilot volume

scale: The same agent pattern fits credit notes and supplier onboarding, which use the same three systems.
Three sister companies run the same ERP; the tools are configuration, not code, per company.

alternatives.headline: Rules catch the easy third. Nothing today **explains** the rest.
criteria: Keeps a person in the decision
alternatives.difference: Products in this market match numbers. This one reads the conversation around the numbers, which is where two thirds of the answers are, and it leaves the release with the clerk.

demo.headline: Three minutes, one invoice, no slides

items.title: A blocked invoice arrives
items.detail: The inbox shows it with the cause already named: price differs on line 3.

items.title: The evidence
items.detail: Order, receipt and the supplier's email side by side, the differing line highlighted.

items.title: The proposal
items.detail: The agent proposes to accept the new price and quotes the email that agreed it.

items.title: The approval
items.detail: The clerk approves. The invoice is released and the reason is logged.

items.title: The hard one
items.detail: An exception the agent cannot settle: it asks the buyer one question in chat.

adoption.headline: A clerk is useful with it in the **first ten minutes**
adoption.lead: No new system to learn: the inbox replaces the ERP list the clerks already work from.

items.title: Open the inbox
items.detail: Single sign-on, the clerk's own exceptions, sorted by due date.

items.title: Read one proposal
items.detail: Cause, evidence, proposed fix. Every claim links to its source document.

items.title: Approve or correct
items.detail: A correction teaches nothing silently: it is logged and reviewed weekly.

items.title: Fall back any time
items.detail: The ERP screen stays available. Nothing is taken away on day one.

facts.label: new logins or installs for the clerk
facts.source: single sign-on through the company directory

roadmap.headline: A working slice in three weeks, real invoices in ten

items.gate: 20 synthetic exceptions resolved with the right cause in at least 17
Time to a decision under one hour on real cases
Finance controller signs off the audit trail

items.name: Completeness and feasibility
evidence: One exception type works end to end on synthetic data
The architecture names every IBM component and what is mocked
A three-phase plan with a gate after each phase
items.gap: The ERP adapter is designed, not built.

items.name: Creativity and innovation
evidence: The agent reads the email thread, not only the numbers
Two agents so that a single tool can write
items.gap: No patent or market search was done.

items.name: Design and usability
evidence: The clerk works in one inbox and approves with one click
Every claim links to the document it came from
items.gap: Tested with one clerk so far.

items.name: Effectiveness and efficiency
evidence: Three days to twenty minutes on the timed cases
The same pattern covers credit notes and onboarding
items.gap: Discount capture is an assumption until treasury confirms.

items.risk: The agent names the wrong cause
items.mitigation: The clerk approves every release; wrong causes are logged and reviewed weekly.

items.risk: Supplier emails carry instructions aimed at the agent
items.mitigation: Email text is quoted as evidence and never followed; the release tool takes its amount from the ERP, not from the email.

items.risk: The ERP adapter takes longer than planned
items.mitigation: The pilot starts read-only; release stays manual until the adapter is proven.

assumptions.text: Six in ten exceptions can be closed without the buyer
assumptions.check: Label 50 past exceptions by hand: was the answer already in the documents?
Ask treasury for the discounts offered and taken in the last quarter.

assumptions.text: A clerk approves the first exception within ten minutes
assumptions.check: Time two clerks on the proof of concept in week 3.
